options: A community held at a stage before the natural climax by human activity such as grazing
A succession that reaches its natural climax community
The earliest pioneer stage of succession
A succession occurring entirely underwater
questions.explain: Continued human or animal interference, such as grazing or mowing, stops succession reaching its natural climax.

questions.q: In the nitrogen cycle, which process converts atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or ammonium ions?
options: Nitrogen fixation
Denitrification
Nitrification
Ammonification
questions.explain: Nitrogen fixation, carried out by bacteria such as Rhizobium and Azotobacter, converts N2 into ammonia.

questions.q: Which genus of bacteria fixes nitrogen within the root nodules of leguminous plants?
options: Nitrosomonas
Pseudomonas
Rhizobium
Nitrobacter
questions.explain: Rhizobium lives mutualistically in legume root nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

questions.q: Which equation correctly expresses net primary productivity (NPP)?
options: NPP = respiratory losses - GPP
NPP = GPP + respiratory losses
NPP = GPP x trophic efficiency
NPP = GPP - respiratory losses
questions.explain: NPP is the energy left for growth after the producers' respiratory losses are subtracted from GPP.

questions.q: Insects limit water loss from their tracheal system mainly by:
options: Increasing ventilation by abdominal pumping
Closing the spiracles using valves and hairs
Using haemoglobin to carry oxygen in the blood
Producing surfactant in the tracheoles
questions.explain: Spiracles can be closed by valves, reducing the evaporative water loss that would otherwise occur from the moist tracheal lining.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prezygotic reproductive isolating mechanism?
options: Death of the hybrid embryo
Differences in courtship behaviour preventing mating
Hybrid breakdown in later generations
Hybrid sterility
questions.explain: Behavioural (courtship) isolation prevents mating, acting before a zygote can form, so it is prezygotic.

questions.q: The semilunar (aortic and pulmonary) valves open when:
options: Ventricular pressure exceeds the pressure in the aorta and pulmonary artery
The ventricles relax during diastole
The AV valves are also open
Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
questions.explain: Once ventricular pressure rises above arterial pressure the semilunar valves open and blood is ejected.

questions.q: In the mark-release-recapture method, the Lincoln index estimates population size N using which expression?
options: N = first marked + second sample - recaptured marked
N = recaptured marked / (first marked x second sample)
N = (first marked + second sample) / 2
N = (first marked x second sample) / recaptured marked
questions.explain: Population = (number first marked x total in second sample) / number marked in the second sample.

questions.q: Fetal haemoglobin has a dissociation curve to the LEFT of adult haemoglobin because:
options: It must release oxygen more readily to the placenta
It is less saturated at every partial pressure of oxygen
It has a higher affinity for oxygen, allowing it to load oxygen from maternal blood at the placenta
It carries less oxygen overall
questions.explain: A higher oxygen affinity (curve to the left) lets fetal Hb take up oxygen from maternal Hb across the placenta.

questions.q: Compared with elastic recoil in expiration, why are the walls of arteries elastic?
options: To slow blood flow for absorption
To stretch under high pressure and recoil, smoothing out pressure surges and maintaining flow
To enable exchange of materials with tissues
To allow active contraction that pumps blood
questions.explain: Elastic tissue in artery walls stretches during systole and recoils during diastole, evening out pulsatile pressure and sustaining blood flow.

questions.q: Glucose is absorbed across the ileum epithelium into the blood by:
options: Facilitated diffusion at the apical membrane independent of sodium
Simple diffusion only, down its concentration gradient
Active transport directly using ATP at the apical membrane
Co-transport with sodium ions, the Na+ gradient being maintained by a sodium-potassium pump
questions.explain: Na+/glucose co-transporters move glucose against its gradient using the Na+ gradient set up by the Na+/K+ pump on the basal membrane.

options: No change in allele frequencies
Both extremes being favoured over the mean
The mean phenotype being favoured
The population mean shifting towards one extreme phenotype
questions.explain: Directional selection favours one extreme, shifting the population mean in that direction over time.
